A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TOHA and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The extensive reorganization and benchmark renaming can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-detection experiments, transfer evaluations, timing measurements, feature comparisons, and human-versus-GPT-4o annotation results.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, transfer and sensitivity experiments, attention-feature ablations, timing measurements, and annotation-validation results.

M1.justification: Both versions compute normalized H0 topological divergence through a minimum spanning forest, rank heads by hallucinated-versus-grounded score differences, select up to six heads using validation ROC-AUC, and average their scores at inference. Revisions to probe and validation data usage concern experimental settings; no new TOHA scoring component is introduced.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on XSum summarization and removes RAGTruth Data2txt, eliminating the data-to-text task. CoQA and SQuAD remain. MS MARCO and CNN/DM + Recent News identify the retained RAGTruth QA and summarization benchmarks, rather than additional newly introduced datasets.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add Haloscope, LLM-Check, and perplexity while removing linear and attention-pooling probes. INSIDE becomes EigenScore, and tokenwise entropy, already maximally aggregated in v1, becomes max entropy. Appendix D also replaces hidden-state combination comparisons with additional sparsity, entropy, spectral-norm, Wasserstein-distance, and attention-to-<s> comparators.

E3.justification: v1 describes RAGTruth QA training data divided into three probe/validation parts; v2 identifies validation with the combined probe sets and specifies 150 annotated samples. SQuAD evaluation expands from two models to all five, and LLaMA-3.1 CoQA samples change from 190 hallucinated/247 grounded to 189/200. New experiments vary probe size, probe-source dataset, and <s> inclusion; XSum annotation bypasses the QA Rouge-L filter.

E4.justification: v2 adds probe-size sensitivity curves, a <s>-removal ablation, and tests of alternative metrics for selecting transferable heads (Figure 4, Table 3, Figure 8). It expands attention-feature comparisons while dropping hidden-state combinations. The earlier multi-model transfer comparisons against supervised probes are replaced by a Mistral-only matrix that varies TOHA's probe-source dataset.

E5.justification: v2 adds uncertainty values throughout the main ROC-AUC tables and states that results are averaged over five runs. v1 reports point estimates there, although annotation and timing uncertainties were already present. Conversely, v2 omits the earlier timing error bars and explicit ten-iteration/three-warmup disclosure. The PDFs do not establish an increase from a known earlier benchmark run count.

E6.justification: The main result tables are substantially revised: for example, Mistral QA/MS MARCO TOHA changes from 0.720 to 0.76 ± 0.04, and LLaMA-2-13B CoQA from 0.800 to 0.93 ± 0.03. Changed evaluation settings prevent interpreting these as matched-setting gains. Numerous ablation and transfer results are added or replaced, while annotation-validation Table 7 remains numerically unchanged. v2 Tables 1 and 3 also have an unexplained model-score mismatch for the with-<s> baselines.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition 3.1(3), characterizing zero divergence through response-to-prompt forest connections with attention weights equal to one, with a brief proof in Appendix B. The earlier MSF identity, bounds, continuity result, exact sequence, and associated proofs are retained or relocated. The original manifold quotient-space derivation is condensed.

C1.justification: v2 removes the stated contribution of releasing two annotated QA datasets and the specific conclusion about outperforming supervised probes under transfer. It introduces the quantified claim that 50 annotations suffice and makes the importance of <s> part of the conclusion. The central TOHA detector and transferability claims remain, but the contribution package shifts substantially toward data efficiency and attention mechanisms.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the entanglement explanation with a stronger interpretation of <s> as a critical detection indicator and interprets alternative-metric experiments as supporting MTop-Div's transferability. New limitations discuss correct-context assumptions, architecture dependence, and multimodal applicability. Appendix G additionally identifies attention-manipulation attacks and overconfidence in TOHA scores, extending beyond v1's general impact discussion.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the 60/15/25 split, ripser++ implementation, SelfCheckGPT's NLI variant, LLM-Check's attention variant, Haloscope's tuning/data procedure, XSum annotation instructions, and artifact licenses. The listed anonymous repository endpoint changes. Conversely, the earlier LightAutoML identification for auxiliary classifiers and annotated-dataset release commitment disappear. Newly disclosed settings do not alone establish that existing experiments changed.

R1.justification: Related work substantively repositions TOHA against limited-label Haloscope and attention-based LLM-Check, emphasizing a gap in training-free structural attention analysis. New references include Du et al., Sriramanan et al., and Barbero et al. on first-token attention, alongside sources supporting alternative features. The earlier evaluation-landscape subsection and several associated citations are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, method explanation, experimental narrative, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, theoretical statements are reorganized between the main text and Appendix B, and dedicated limitations and additional appendices are introduced. These changes substantially reshape the document's narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, Figure 3 replaces head heatmaps with pairwise scatterplots, and new robustness and alternative-metric displays appear. Main tables gain single-generation indicators and uncertainty columns; transfer and timing tables give way to different graphical displays. The hallucination illustration is reduced and moved into the main text, and the appendices change from predominantly single-column to two-column layout.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports TOHA's practical, limited-label use through relevant new baselines, probe-size and metric ablations, five-run reporting, and explicit applicability limits. These improve validation and transparency beyond v1. The net gain is limited by losing data-to-text and multi-model supervised-transfer evidence, and by the unexplained model-score mismatch between v2 Tables 1 and 3, which weakens confidence in the new token ablation.
